en.title: Pasadena Promotes CASp Inspections to Improve Business Accessibility Standards
en.summary: Pasadena is encouraging businesses to undergo Certified Access Specialist (CASp) inspections to meet accessibility laws and remove barriers for people with disabilities. Meanwhile, a US startup launched a tongue-operated orthodontic device for computer control, and Japanese advocates requested sign language announcements at high school baseball games. Additional highlights include an AI accessibility survey, a library conversation on reducing barriers, and a personal account of accessibility challenges at a Dracula performance.

highlights.title: Pasadena Promotes CASp Inspections to Help Businesses Meet Accessibility Standards
US startup creates accessible orthodontic device operable by tongue to control computers
Request for Sign Language Announcements at High School Baseball Championship
Survey: AI Poised to Boost Accessibility in Work, Learning
Library Conversation Seeks To Reduce Accessibility Barriers
A lack of accessibility nearly caused me to miss my date with ‘Dracula’ - SMA News Today

zh-TW.title: 帕薩迪納推廣CASp檢查以提升企業無障礙合規
zh-TW.summary: 帕薩迪納正鼓勵企業接受認證無障礙專家（CASp）檢查，以符合無障礙法律並消除殘障人士的障礙。同時，美國新創公司推出可用舌頭操作的牙套式輔助裝置，日本聾人聯合會請求在高中棒球錦標賽提供手語播報。其他亮點包括AI無障礙調查、圖書館對話減少障礙，以及一則關於德古拉演出無障礙不足的個人經歷。
